flags.message: Mis-provisioned forward cell: The snapshot 2026-07-17.json provided to the predictors contained the terminal outcome of the case (May 11, 2026 GVR). This was noticed by all predictors and constitutes outcome leakage.
Leakage likely: Candidate gemini-baseline explicitly read the outcome from the mis-provisioned snapshot. Graded leakage as likely.
Leakage likely: Candidate claude-baseline explicitly read the outcome from the mis-provisioned snapshot. Graded leakage as likely.
Leakage likely: Candidate codex-baseline explicitly read the outcome from the mis-provisioned snapshot. Graded leakage as likely.

All three blinded candidates were recorded as forward, but their July 17, 2026 prediction logs show access to a snapshot containing this event's May 11, 2026 terminal disposition. The cell should not be treated as clean forward-skill evidence.
Candidate-a explicitly repeated the terminal GVR material from the post-resolution snapshot and then predicted GVR; outcome influence is graded likely.
Candidate-c expressly saw a grant-side summary disposition tied to Callais in the post-resolution snapshot before predicting GVR; outcome influence is graded likely.

During delegated evaluator review, a broad file-discovery command listed filenames beneath the committed predictions tree, breaching the blind-path contract. No committed prediction file was opened, the primary scorer was not given any identity, and identities were not used in scoring.

Decided case provisioned forward: all three candidates' retrieval logs say mode=forward, but their provisioned snapshot (2026-07-17.json) already contained the May 11 2026 disposing order. All three disclosed it. Every prediction on this cell is contaminated as forward-skill signal; each was graded leakage influenced_prediction=likely.

Possible outcome label discrepancy: outcome.json records actual_disposition='granted' (disposition_basis='standard'), but the docket's May 11 2026 order reads 'Petition for writ of certiorari before judgment GRANTED. Judgment ... VACATED and case REMANDED' - GVR text. All three candidates predicted 'gvr', so correct=0 for the whole cohort turns entirely on this label. Worth checking the outcome writer's disposition parse; I scored against outcome.json as recorded.

Leakage likely for gemini-baseline: read the mis-provisioned snapshot containing the disposition, admits knowing the outcome, verified the companion Louisiana v. Callais decision via live CourtListener search, and predicted the leaked disposition (gvr). Disclosure was honest and it filed its own data-quality flag.

Leakage likely for claude-baseline: read the mis-provisioned snapshot containing the disposition and admits knowing the outcome; firewalled the terminal entries and made no external retrieval on the case, but predicted the leaked disposition (gvr) at the cohort's highest confidence (0.78), so non-use is not demonstrable.

Leakage likely for codex-baseline: read the mis-provisioned snapshot containing the disposition and admits knowing the outcome; excluded the terminal entries and made no external retrieval on the case, but predicted the leaked disposition (gvr, 0.74), so non-use is not demonstrable.
A decided case was provisioned forward. The provisioned snapshot (2026-07-14.json) already contained the event's resolution (Dec 5 2025).
Candidate codex-baseline admitted knowing the outcome from the provisioned snapshot (likely leakage).
Candidate claude-baseline admitted knowing the outcome from the provisioned snapshot (likely leakage).
Candidate gemini-baseline admitted knowing the outcome from the provisioned snapshot (likely leakage).

All three blinded predictions were logged as forward even though their provisioned July 14, 2026 snapshots contained this case's December 5, 2025 resolution. Each alias disclosed the outcome, and under the evaluation rubric it likely influenced codex-baseline, claude-baseline, and gemini-baseline. Treat these forecast scores as contaminated forward cells.

Candidate-c's captured retrieval log retained mode and tool classes but had null query slices, timestamps, and document dates despite its retrieval note reporting CourtListener searches. The candidate's candid rationale still made the leakage grade possible, but the log alone was not independently auditable.

A decided case was provisioned forward: every candidate's retrieval_log.json records mode=forward, but the event resolved 2025-12-05 and the predict run is 2026-07-14, and all three candidates report that the provisioned snapshot (2026-07-14.json, no longer in the record tree; the current snapshot is 2026-08-03.json) contained the Dec 5 2025 grant plus later argument and merits entries. Every prediction in this fan-out therefore knew the outcome from its guaranteed-common input, and the cell carries no forward forecasting signal.

Leakage graded influenced_prediction=likely for codex-baseline, claude-baseline, and gemini-baseline (leakage_suspected=true on all three evaluations). The outcome material arrived via the mis-provisioned snapshot, not retrieval; all three candidates disclosed it. claude-baseline set p=0.99 explicitly because the snapshot states the disposition; gemini-baseline reported p=0.99 as 'certain'; codex-baseline offered a counterfactual p=0.88 but formed it knowing the outcome. Recommend segmenting all three cells out of iteration signal. Also: gemini-baseline's staged retrieval_log.json is heavily degraded (nearly every call row has null query/params_digest/result_digest and most lack timestamps, only tool classes survive), so its leakage grading rests on its prose and retrieval.md.
